notes.title: Shared Namespace Residue Remains in Manhunt
notes.problem: Production Manhunt code still contains naming inherited from the shared Dark Crystal implementation. Current behavior is internally consistent, so no gameplay failure is claimed.
notes.action: Rename shared and domain-specific identifiers so Manhunt ownership is unambiguous.

evidence.finding: Production identifiers, log prefixes, and runtime structures retain DarkCrystal/shared naming inside the Manhunt implementation.

notes.title: Developer Script-Event Authorization Is Not Centralized
notes.problem: State-mutating developer/admin script events, including database and Manhunt reset surfaces, do not consistently pass through one explicit internal authorization owner. Ordinary-player command reachability is not claimed.
notes.action: Route every developer/admin world or persistent-state mutation through one canonical permission service.

evidence.finding: database:reset, manhunt reset/debug, and arena-party developer mutation handlers do not share an explicit internal authorization gate.

notes.title: Hunter Count Scaling Is Explicit but Highly Non-Monotonic
notes.problem: The hard-coded player-count table changes Hunter count non-monotonically: 8→2, 9→3, 10→2, 11→1, 12→3, 13→1, 14→2, 15→3, 16→2. The current Guide does not define this scaling, so no gameplay bug is claimed.
notes.action: Confirm the intended Hunter-count curve with game design and document it as one canonical balancing rule.

evidence.finding: ku/Di() contains the explicit 2–16 player Hunter-count table.

notes.title: Chase Duration Scales with Hunter Count but Is Undocumented in the Guide
notes.problem: The base 4:30 chase duration is multiplied to 90% for two Hunters and 80% for three Hunters. This implementation is coherent but is not described by the current Guide.
notes.action: Confirm and document Hunter-count-dependent chase duration if it is intended balancing.

evidence.finding: bu()/na() apply 1.0, 0.9, or 0.8 timeout factors according to Hunter count.

notes.title: Health Regen Subsystem Is Present but Has No Authored Spawn Locations
notes.problem: A complete Health Regen subsystem remains in production, but every arena receives regenLocations from an empty base list. Current survivorHealth is also 1, so no current gameplay failure is claimed.
notes.action: Remove the inactive subsystem/configuration if obsolete, or provide approved locations and health design if it is intended to return.

evidence.finding: Dp=[] feeds regenLocations for all six arenas while regen timers/entities/messages remain implemented.

notes.title: Additional Honey Trap Pickup Subsystem Has No Authored Spawn Locations
notes.problem: Periodic Honey Trap pickup logic remains implemented, but every arena receives trapPickupLocations from an empty base list. Initial Runner traps still function, so this is not promoted as a gameplay bug.
notes.action: Remove the inactive pickup subsystem or provide approved pickup locations if additional trap pickups are intended.

evidence.finding: Rp=[] feeds trapPickupLocations for all six arenas while pickup spawn/collection logic remains implemented.

notes.title: Legacy Multi-Health Tag Messaging Remains While Survivor Health Is One
notes.problem: Messages and health-oriented support code still describe remaining health/tag cooldown behavior, while current survivorHealth=1 makes a valid Hunter tag an immediate elimination. The selected Guide does not establish that multi-hit health is required.
notes.action: Remove or simplify legacy multi-health messaging/code if one-hit elimination is the approved design, or restore an explicit multi-hit design if intended.

evidence.finding: survivorHealth=1 coexists with corruptionHitTagger/corruptionHitTarget healthRemaining messaging and Health Regen support.
